problem: The stated ciphertext XSEEMA has six letters, but the plaintext EXAMS has five and the chapter itself says the ciphertext is split as 2, 2, 1. Column 2 gives X, S; column 1 gives E, M; column 3 gives A, so the ciphertext is five letters. A student following the worked steps cannot get XSEEMA, which makes the example look wrong.
fix: Reading in key order (column 2, column 1, column 3) gives XS + EM + A = XSEMA. The receiver splits the 5 letters as 2, 2, 1, refills the columns and reads the rows back to EXAMS.

where: Section 2, first paragraph after the affine formula
problem: "a = 2 sends both A (0) and N (13) to 0" is only true when b = 0. With a general b the two letters collide on the value b, not on 0, so the sentence is slightly inaccurate as written.
fix: Write: a = 2 sends both A (0) and N (13) to the same letter, namely the letter numbered b, so the two cannot be told apart after decryption.

where: Section 3, bullet list and example on columnar transposition
problem: "padding the last row if it is short" suggests adding filler letters, but the example then leaves the third cell of row 2 empty and counts only 5 ciphertext letters. A student may add an X as filler and get a different rectangle.
fix: Say clearly: leave the unused cells of the last row empty (no filler letters in this unit); the receiver works out the empty cells from the message length and the rectangle size.
